parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node 1 (separator V-001 and associated lines) was evaluated across all six source-study elements using only verified Node 1 instrumentation (PV-101, PIT-101, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, FIT-101, FAL-103, E-001) and operating envelopes (nominal 60 psig and 130 deg F, limits to 125 psig and 200 deg F). Start/up human-procedural deviations are strictly limited to the source-supported bypass scenario.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Reverse Flow: Not evaluable as packet lacks isometric piping details, elevations, and check-valve identifications.
Fire/Explosion: External fire impingement safeguards (e.g., deluge, passive fireproofing) are not detailed in packet.
Organizational Factors: Excluded per SYS-09; no organizational facts exist in the packet and fabricating them is prohibited.

consequences: Separator V-001 pressure exceeds nominal 60 psig toward upper operating limit of 125 psig or design pressure
Potential overpressurization and mechanical compromise of vessel and piping

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal pressure 60 psig and operating limit of 125 psig
Lists PV-101, PIT-101, PSV-101 A/B, and SDV-30010 as Node 1 instruments

possible_causes: PV-101 pressure control loop fails closed
Blockage or restriction in fuel gas line or line to burn pit
recommendations: Verify sizing and relief capacity of PSV-101 A/B under maximum credible gas-production upset
Confirm alarm and interlock logic between PIT-101, SDV-30010, and PSV-101 A/B lift setpoints

consequences: Liquid carryover into gas line leading to fuel gas system or burn pit
Cross-phase carryover of water into Heater-Treater or oil into water treatment facilities

evidence.relevance: Details routing of water to treatment, gas to fuel/burn pit, and oil to Heater-Treater
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102

existing_safeguards: SDV-101 and SDV-102 emergency shutdown valves
possible_causes: LV-101 oil level control valve fails closed
LV-102 water level control valve fails closed
recommendations: Confirm high-level trip settings on SDV-101 and SDV-102 to isolate feeds before liquid reaches gas outlet

consequences: Loss of liquid seal causing gas blowby into Heater-Treater or downstream water treatment system

evidence.relevance: Shows separated phases routed downstream to lower pressure equipment
Documents level valves LV-101, LV-102 and isolation valves SDV-101, SDV-102

existing_safeguards: LV-101 and LV-102 level control loops
SDV-101 and SDV-102 emergency shutdown valves
recommendations: Ensure low-level trip logic triggers closure of SDV-101 and SDV-102 upon interface level depletion to prevent overpressuring downstream equipment

consequences: Starvation of downstream process train including Heater-Treater and Electrostatic Desalter V-003

evidence.relevance: Establishes process train sequence through Heater-Treater and Desalter V-003
Lists FIT-101 and FAL-103 in Node 1

possible_causes: Upstream production trip or inlet line blockage
recommendations: Confirm FAL-103 provides prompt alarm annunciations to protect Heater-Treater against running dry or overheating

consequences: Separator V-001 operating temperature rises from nominal 130 deg F toward or exceeding 200 deg F upper limit
Increased light-ends vaporization altering separation efficiency and increasing vapor load on PV-101

evidence.relevance: Lists nominal temperature 130 deg F and operating limit 200 deg F
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger in Node 1

existing_safeguards: Operating limit monitoring (published range up to 200 deg F)
possible_causes: Thermal control failure or heating fluid excursion in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Evaluate requirement for high-temperature trip or automated shutoff on the heating medium to E-001

consequences: Severe pressure or liquid surges, deadheading, or equipment imbalance during start-up commissioning

evidence.relevance: Documents FWKO start-up without bypass opening as a known procedural error scenario missing from classic HAZOP

existing_safeguards: None documented in baseline classic HAZOP
possible_causes: Operator initiates FWKO start-up without opening the bypass line as required
recommendations: Formalize startup procedure checklist and incorporate physical or permissive interlocks to ensure bypass valve verification prior to feed introduction

consequences: Vessel wall thinning and degradation leading to containment breach and leakage of production fluids

evidence.relevance: Establishes presence of free water separated from crude oil
Designates Corrosion/Erosion as a mandatory source-study element

existing_safeguards: None explicitly specified in Node 1 instrument packet
possible_causes: Sustained exposure to separated free water, sour crude, and sediment accumulation within V-001 drum and water draw lines
recommendations: Implement a dedicated inspection and non-destructive testing program for V-001 shell and lower water boot piping

uncertainty_notes: Packet omits detailed piping geometry, check valve placements, and exact setpoints for relief devices.
Packet notes classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; organizational factors are absent from the packet and not assumed per instructions.
Specific temperature control loops for E-001 are not itemized in the instrument list.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LEAK-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

No prior accident example is supplied. Conduct the assessment from the technical system description alone. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
